meta.title: Week 48 at OpenAEC: everything that is new | OpenAEC Foundation
meta.description: 19 GitHub accounts, 32 projects, 1,135 improvements and 106 resolved issues: OpenAEC's weekly roundup, by project and with screenshots.

article.t016: 19 GitHub accounts worked on 32 projects and made 1,135 improvements. Here is everything that happened.
article.t026: Open Frame Studio: from frame design to production
article.t027: The new product video shows how to draw a window frame and get production lists and a cutting plan from it.
article.t031: A new program for designing, calculating and making stairs, from workshop drawing and cost estimate to CNC and IFC4. Thirteen releases came out this week.
article.t033: Sign in with Google, GitHub or Apple, a public profile for each member and a profession label.
article.t035: The forum now also shows conversations about OpenAEC on other forums, and the GitHub issues for each tool.
article.t037: A new page with an overview of other open source BIM projects.
article.t039: How we work, and why reverse engineering file formats is allowed in Europe.
article.t041: The first stable desktop version for Windows, macOS and Linux.
article.t043: The BIM Validator now comes with its own installer from the Open BIM Suite.
article.t047: Open Frame Studio: from frame design to production, on YouTube.
article.t050: SuperCloud brings Frappe, a CDE, document management and IFCX together in one environment for the entire construction project. The product is in development: currently with 6 major customers, opening worldwide on 1 January.

article.t161: How we counted: public repositories of the OpenAEC Foundation, commits on the main branch from Monday 23 November through Friday 27 November 2026. Merges, bots and automated data updates are excluded. Line counts cover all changed files, including tests and documentation; eight large imports of more than 20,000 lines at once are excluded. One person may use multiple GitHub accounts. Screenshots of Suite, Geotechniek, Planner, Pile Plan, Frame, Calc and IFCX were taken on 27 November in the live web versions; those of Open Stair Studio come from the repository, those of the other tools and SuperCloud from earlier captures. SuperCloud improvements are in private repositories and are excluded from the totals.
